title: Heap-residue accumulation causing intermittent GPU OOMs and KV cache corruption — runtime recovery & fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted and Dedicated reported sudden GPU OOM waves accompanied by KV-index miss patterns and occasional session-level corruption. Investigation shows a slow accumulation of small inaccessible arena allocations ("heap residue") that prevents slab compaction and eventually starves page allocation under kernel pressure. The incident surface affects hosted burst nodes and Dedicated heavy-chat customers during long-tailed sessions.
impact: High — P0. Customers observed degraded throughput (>3x latency), elevated reject rates, and 2 customer escalations with business impact. Risk of data loss is low but session churn increases and some sessions require restart.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create long-lived chat sessions with repeated small prefills and streaming tokens for 45+ minutes
2) Enable prefix caching and set KV cache per-session watermark low (default)
3) Load synthetic multi-tenant traffic with interleaved short/long sequences at high concurrency
4) Observe GC/evictor effectiveness degrade and GPU OOMs after 60-90 minutes; KV index shows tombstone growth and pointer skew
observations: - Memory profiler shows many ~32-512B unreachable shards in arenas (heap residue) that are not reclaimed by normal compactor runs
- Evictor metrics: per-session cache size stable but free pages on slab pools decline steadily
- KV index reports incremental tombstone count increase correlated with evict pauses
- OOMs are noisy on nodes running mixed tenant workloads with large and small model inference concurrently
root_cause: A coordination gap between the async tombstone reclaimer and the arena compaction pass: small freed handles from session churn were marked tombstoned but not reclaimed quickly, leading to fragmentation inside arena extents. The GPU allocator's page pinning heuristic preferred contiguous allocations and failed to pack small holes, resulting in effective memory pressure and preemptive OOMs under bursty allocation patterns.
proposed_fix: 1) Fast-path: roll a minimal runtime hotpatch that adds an aggressive background compaction trigger when per-node free-page ratio drops below threshold. 2) Medium-term: implement bounded per-session cache watermarks + async tombstone foregrounding to reclaim small freed handles sooner. 3) Long-term: add arena slab-squeeze pass that coalesces small residues during low-util windows and adjust kernel page-pinning heuristics to tolerate micro-fragmentation.
mitigation_steps_taken: - Deployed canary hotpatch to hosted region eu-west-1 with background compaction and observed immediate recovery of free pages
- Applied customer-side mitigation: advised Dedicated customers to set session cache watermark to lower value and restart affected node pools while patch rolls
- Increased alert sensitivity for tombstone growth and free-page ratio across clusters
rollout_plan: 1) Canary (eu-west-1 hosted, 5% traffic) — rolling patch 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC
2) Monitor 48h, validate OOM rate, throughput and latency (SLO delta <5%)
3) Gradual 50% expansion to all hosted regions and a dedicated capacity pilot (2026-03-14)
4) Ship medium-term change (async tombstone foreground) behind runtime flag for 2026-03-20
5) Long-term slab-squeeze design to land in runtime-1.22 with perf tests and canary rollout
rollback_plan: Revert runtime hotpatch and restore previous compactor schedule; for Dedicated, revert flags and instruct capacity restarts. Keep accelerated observability enabled for 72h post-rollback.
qa_plan: - Add stress test in CI that simulates long-lived sessions with small-churn allocations for 2 hours
- Inject fault tests that pause tombstone reclaimer and assert compactor triggers run within 120s
- Run GPU OOM fuzz harness across model suite (gpt-small, gpt-medium) under mixed-concurrency profiles
monitoring_and_sla_checks: - Dashboards: rapid filter by deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), tenant, and model family
- Alerts: P1 when node_free_page_ratio < 12% AND kvcache_tombstone_rate rising for 10m
- Postmortem: attach perf graphs and customer timeline within 72h of resolution
